title: Carrier
description: One carrier folder's carrier.json: the single source of truth for that carrier. scripts/generate-api-contract.mjs merges every carriers/*/carrier.json into contracts/openapi.json under x-carriers and regenerates the TypeScript, Swift and package catalogs from it.

id.description: Carrier id; must equal the folder name and appears in CarrierId.

displayNames.description: Localized names, keyed by locale. Only carriers whose name is translated define this.

aliases.description: Other names the carrier is known by. The carrier pickers search them.

region.description: Where the carrier delivers under its own name, home country first. The carrier pickers show and search these countries. Empty for networks without a home market (UPS, FedEx) and for platforms.

color.description: Accent color used by the web and native clients.

selectable.description: Whether the carrier appears in the manual carrier picker.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used when the carrier reports local timestamps without an offset.

mode.description: automatic: we fetch tracking ourselves. link-only: we can only link to the portal.

adapter.description: "universal", the id of a carrier folder that has adapter.ts (its own, or the folder whose adapter serves it), or null for link-only carriers.

upstreamName.description: Carrier name as the serving adapter's upstream service spells it, when it differs from displayName.

requirements.description: Extra inputs the forms collect besides the tracking number. Each is required unless it is marked optional.

steps.description: Ordered runner steps. Reserved for the runner phase; empty means the adapter still owns its own flow.

recognition.description: Present when the adapter implements recognize(): a cheap check, without the user's inputs, of whether the carrier knows a number (plain HTTP, a clean not-found, no browser). Ambiguous numbers ask these carriers. rank orders them by how common they are for the app's users, highest first; no two carriers share a rank.

pattern.description: Regular expression for the normalized numbers recognize() can answer. Recognition is only asked about those; a number another rule offers stays a suggestion. Absent: every number the carrier's rules offer.

servedCountriesOnly.description: Recognition asks the carrier only when the caller's country hint is one of its countries: its numbers are bare runs that carriers elsewhere print too. Absent: asked whatever the hint.

localClocks.description: True when the adapter can return scans without an instant: a wall clock with no UTC offset, or provider text. Consumers can keep that history beside instants and ask fallback providers for dated scans.

dateOnlyScans.description: True when every scan the adapter dates by its day alone is one the carrier gives no clock by design, such as a delivery round or a history listed under day headings. Fallback providers have no clock to add to such a scan.

browser.description: True when a lookup through the adapter can open a browser: the private browser service or a local or remote Chromium. Consumers can space out repeated lookups.

browserRecognition.description: Present when the adapter implements recognizeWithBrowser(): opt-in browser confirmation without recipient inputs, requiring dated shipment activity. Higher rank is asked first after HTTP checks are inconclusive; no two carriers share a browser rank.

capabilities.description: Declared capability flags. Reserved for a later phase.

portal.description: Facts about the carrier's public tracking portal.

searchUrl.description: Public page, with no number in it, where a visitor on a phone types a tracking number. Linked when the number is hidden. Left out when the carrier has no such page.

helpUrl.description: The carrier's official page where someone receiving a parcel gets help or reaches its customer service. Linked when a parcel stops moving. Left out when the carrier has no such page.

hidesDestinationLeg.description: Regular expression: numbers whose journey in the destination country the portal does not show, as it names no carrier there. Linked readers are told so when such a parcel stops moving.

siteName.description: Name of the site the portal URL points at, when it is not the carrier itself.

canaryUrl.description: Public, credential-free HTTPS URL the weekly canary probes. Required for automatic carriers.

shows.description: Fields the portal displays. Reserved for a later documentation phase.

scraped.description: Fields we retain. Reserved for a later documentation phase.

discarded.description: Fields the portal shows that we deliberately drop. Reserved for a later documentation phase.

unavailable.description: Fields the portal does not expose. Reserved for a later documentation phase.

links.description: Rules that recognize a carrier tracking link pasted by the user.

detection.description: Rules that recognize a tracking number. Exactly one high-confidence match selects the carrier.

field.description: Input name. The generator checks that the validator is one this input accepts.

whenTrackingNumber.description: Regular expression: the input is only asked for and validated for matching tracking numbers.

optional.description: The user may leave the input blank: the adapter tracks without it and uses it only to unlock extra detail. A value that is supplied is still validated.

showsMore.description: With optional: the carrier shows more of the parcel with the input, whatever else answers, so a parcel saved without it is worth asking for it. Left out where the carrier needs it for only some parcels of the shape and asks for those.

readsCountry.description: With a postcode: the lookup reads the country the postcode is from (postcodeCountry), so it is worth naming beside the postcode. Left out where the carrier reads the postcode alone.

id.description: Stable rule id, unique across the catalog; the sweep, the collision file and checksumRejections refer to it.

preferred.description: Low-confidence rules only: the number shape is evidence for this carrier (such as a depot range), so it is listed first among the suggestions. It never selects the carrier on its own.
